headline: Stocks fell a fourth day Tuesday (S&P 500 -1.0%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Dow -1.6%) on software AI-replacement fears (Salesforce -9%) and tech outage worries. Nvidia beat after the close and guided Q4 to about $130B, rising about 4% after hours. 10-year yield 5.11%; a December Fed hike is priced in.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. A 10-year yield above 5% and a likely December Fed hike remain a mild headwind.
No clear US sector news. Telecoms are defensive, but bond yields above 5% compete with their dividends.
October retail sales showed auto dealers -1.6% and furniture -2.3%, and markets price a December Fed hike with the 10-year near 5.1%, which hurts homes, cars and furniture.
Energizer jumped 12.6% on strong results, but import prices rose 1.1% in October, squeezing costs. Walmart and Target results this week set the tone.
Disney fell 1.5% despite revenue up 16% and a 33% dividend raise. Consumer spending is still solid but the saving rate is near a four-year low.
No clear sector news. Steady retail sales help volumes, rising rates raise financing costs.
Nvidia beat (revenue $115.8B, up 103%) and guided Q4 to about $130B vs about $125B expected; Micron and Credo rose after hours. New US AI-chip access limits and Nvidia's CEO vacancy keep risk high.
Energy was the only gaining sector Tuesday, but hopes of diplomacy in the Iran war could cap oil. No clear one-month direction.
Financials were among the weakest Tuesday and crypto names fell (Coinbase -4%, Robinhood -4%) with Bitcoin down over 20% in a month. Higher rates help bank margins but hurt credit.
UnitedHealth fell 5.4% on sweeping anti-fraud proposals for Medicare and Medicaid, which could pressure insurers and providers for weeks. Healthcare was among the weakest sectors.
Healthcare lagged Tuesday, but no broad drug or device news. SELLAS surged on a Phase 3 cancer vaccine win (a single small-cap event).
AECOM rose 11% on a record $28B backlog, a good sign for engineering and infrastructure demand, but one company is not a trend. October industrial production fell 0.4%.
No clear news for this group.
Gold slipped 0.2% to about $3,849. No clear driver for metals and miners this month.
October industrial production fell 0.4% and import prices rose 1.1%, a mixed picture for chemicals and materials makers.
Industrial production fell 0.4% in October and rate-hike bets weigh on capital spending, but AI data-center buildout supports equipment demand.
October retail sales rose 0.2% as expected and the core control group beat (+0.6%), with online sellers +1.2%. Home Depot fell 2.5% on a CEO change. Walmart and Target report this week.
Salesforce fell about 9% and Microsoft 2.3% as fears that AI will replace software products spread; outages at banks and agencies added security worries. Nvidia's beat may help sentiment only partly.
Recent air-travel tech outages are a short-term hit; oil swings on Iran news cut both ways for fuel costs.
Defensive and helped by AI power demand, but a 10-year yield above 5% competes with dividends.

avoid.UNH: Fell 5.4% on sweeping Medicare and Medicaid anti-fraud proposals that could hang over the stock for weeks.
